core_message: Tardigrades can endure the vacuum of space and extreme conditions that kill almost all life.
title: 1500 Species, 10‑Day Space Test: Tardigrades Survive Vacuum
description:
Tardigrades, nicknamed water bears, are tiny eight‑legged creatures that can survive the harshest environments on Earth – and even the vacuum of space.  Discover how these microscopic marvels endure radiation, extreme temperatures and the emptiness beyond our atmosphere.

Key points:
- First described in 1773 and named for their slow walk.
- About 1,500 known species live from mountaintops to the deep sea.
- In 2007, they survived exposure to outer space for days.
- Their resilience comes from a unique “tun” state.

Sources:
- Wikipedia article on Tardigrade
- ESA experiment BIOPAN‑5 (2007)

Based on the Wikipedia article "Tardigrade" (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tardigrade), licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

scenes.narration: The Tun State: Before launch they entered a desiccated “tun” state, retracting their legs and sealing their bodies, which protects them from radiation and dehydration.
scenes.purpose: Explain the biological mechanism behind their survival.
